etymology: From Maranao agama +‎ -han, from Sanskrit आगम (āgama). Compare agham.
notes: Coined by Lupon sa Agham (Committee on Science) in the Maugnaying Talasalitaang Pang-agham : Ingles-Pilipino (Correlative Word List for Sciences : English-Filipino) 2nd edition, published in 1979 and edited by Gonsalo del Rosario. This term fell under the Kublupon sa Batnayan (Subcommittee on Philosophy), headed by Conrado R. Reyes.

etymology: Blend of ag-(agham) +‎ -barog, from Cebuano barog
Blend of agham (“science”) +‎ Cebuano himo (“to make; to construct”).

Borrowed from Maguindanao agimat (“amulet; talisman”) or Tausug adjimat (“amulet; talisman”), from Malay azimat (عزيمة), from Arabic عَزِيمَةْ (ʕazīmat), the informal construct state of عَزِيمَة (ʕazīma).
notes: Compare Maranao adimat. The “amulet; talisman” sense is first attested in c. 1860 via Noceda & Sanlucar, with the term arriving in the Philippines in the first half of the 1800s according to Potet (2013), while the homophonous "thrift; care" sense is attested since c. 1754 also via Noceda & Sanlucar according to Potet (2013). See also Malay jimat (“frugal; prudent; saving money”).
